_about: The spelling facts that convert() and detect() read. Each row maps form, written in the norm era, to value in the norm target. source names the entry of _sources that the row comes from, and for a curated row the group of _groups. A dual AO1990 cell joins its two forms with '|', in source order. curated is true for the 1911 pairs that the backward 1911 pass inverts and that detect() weighs double. A pre-1911 form whose 1911 form no source decides has rows for its AO1990 forms only. The reforma_1911 values do not always have the accents of the 1911 print. A curated value has its AO1990 diacritics (elle gives ele, where the 1911 print writes êle). Where the European and Brazilian norms differ only by an open or closed vowel before a nasal (anónimo, anônimo; cómodo, cômodo), the value is the European form, and the Brazilian edge derives ê and ô by rule. A value from the tugalex archaisms list is its modern pt-PT form (comsigo gives consigo), or its pre-AO1990 form where the AO1990 pt-PT map lists the modern form (architecto gives arquitecto). The 1911 reform kept the c and p of -ct- and -pt- words such as acto, óptimo, director and afecto: affecto gives afecto in 1911, and only the AO1990 edge gives afeto. tools/build_spelling_table.py built the rows with tugalex 2.4.9a1.
_sources: Reforma Ortográfica de 1911 (Portaria de 1 de setembro de 1911), comissão de Gonçalves Viana
Cândido de Figueiredo, Novo Diccionário da Língua Portuguesa (1913)

_groups.ch_k: ch = /k/ -> c (before a/o/u or consonant) or qu (before e/i). The /S/-ch of chave/chuva is untouched and never listed here.
_groups.geminates: Double consonants reduced to single, EXCEPT etymological rr/ss which survive in modern spelling (carro, passo).
_groups.silent_and_h: Etymological silent consonants in mn/ps clusters and medial/initial silent h, dropped in 1911.
_groups.k_w: Loanword k/w regularised to qu/v (or u). The bare foreignisms (whisky, sandwich) are NOT listed, as those spellings remain acceptable today.
